newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore to announce election date on Monday.
newsitem.headline: Singapore to announce election date on Monday.

text.p: Singapore Prime Ministr Goh Chok Tong said on Saturday he would announce a date for general elections on Monday, the closing day for nominations.
"I can tell you on Monday," Goh told reporters when asked when the elections would be.

His People's Action Party (PAP), which has won every election since 1959, is expected to win again by a wide margin. In the parliament dissolved earlier in the week, opposition parties held just four of the 81 elected seats.
Elections have to be held by April. Most analysts and opposition politicians expect them to be held in early January.
Just after parliament was dissolved, the government announced that December 23 would be the last day for nominations of candidates in the elections.
The PAP has helped transform Singapore into one of Asia's most highly developed cities where the per capita Gross Domestic Product (GDP) is higher than that of the former colonial power, Britain.
Political analysts say the PAP does not want to give the opposition parties time to develop campaigns that might eat into its huge majority in parliament.
Goh, speaking to university students on Friday night, was blunt about how the PAP did what it could to keep opposition politicians out of parliament.
"Do you think we could have done even half of what was achieved in the last 30 years if we had a multi-party system and a revolving door government?" he asked.
"Do you think we could have done just as well if we had a government which was constantly being held in check by 10 to 20 opposition members in the last 30 years?"
